answer: Unique-Artifact Consumption Gate. Each identity must submit a freshly generated artifact whose exact byte sequence never recurs, and the gate rejects any resubmission. Agents wander across the artifact space, hunting unused outputs. Admission stores a collision-resistant digest, so reuse fails verification. Attackers must produce one novel valid artifact per sybil, never repeating an opal-like rare result. Cost scales linearly: roughly one compute unit and one storage slot of unique entropy per identity, capping mass registration. A whisper of duplication disqualifies the whole batch.
